name: Zone.Identifier ADS (Mark of the Web)
os_min: Introduced with Internet Explorer; ADS format standardized further by Windows 10
location: Alternate Data Stream on the downloaded file: <filename>:Zone.Identifier:$DATA
purpose: Marks files originating from the internet (or other untrusted zones) so Windows/Office apply extra security prompts (Protected View, SmartScreen).
normal_baseline: Downloaded files carry ZoneId=3 with a HostUrl matching a known, expected source.
anomalies: Executable or script with ZoneId=3 and a HostUrl pointing to a known malicious-tool distribution or paste site
MOTW-bearing file with the Unblock checkbox cleared shortly before execution, indicating deliberate bypass
parsing_tools: dir /r (legacy) or forensic ADS-aware tools (FTK Imager, X-Ways)
anti_forensic_notes: Transferring a file to/from a non-NTFS filesystem (FAT32, network transfer that doesn't preserve ADS, or extraction from certain archive formats) strips the ADS and the mark along with it, so its absence does not prove local origin.
